title: Great Stink
text: The Great Stink was an event in Central London during July and August 1858 in which the hot weather exacerbated the smell of untreated human waste and industrial effluent that was present on the banks of the River Thames. The problem had been mounting for several years, with an ageing and inadequate sewer system that emptied directly into the Thames. It was thought that the miasma from the effluent transmitted contagious diseases, and three outbreaks of cholera before the Great Stink were blamed on the ongoing problems with the river.
